records.numbers_detail: PDF page 314: 'risperidone .25 mg q.h.s. initiated for seven days and then increased to twice daily dosing'; 'risperdal dose of .5 mg three times daily'. PDF page 317: 'risperidone .5 mg b.i.d.'. PDF page 315, figure 4 axis labels also give Risperdal doses (.25 mg q.h.s., .25 mg b.i.d., .25 mg t.i.d., .5 mg t.i.d.).

The book says 'is postulated'.

records.notes: On PDF page 320 the body text says dextromethorphan/quinidine 'shares the attributes of being an uncompetitive NMDA antagonist with memantine'. PDF page 320 also says sigma 1 and SERT binding are present 'in DM/Q but not in memantine'; no record is written for that negative statement.

records.quote: Although the mechanism of action of DM/Q is not fully characterized, its unique properties as an NMDA receptor antagonist and as a Sigma 1 receptor agonist
records.notes: The mechanism is stated for the combination product, not for dextromethorphan or quinidine separately. Other names printed: 'Dextromethorphan and quinidine sulfate (Nuedexta)' (PDF page 303, table 3) and 'AVP-923' (PDF page 320). 'Uncompetitive' is from another sentence on PDF page 320. Drug kind: the book says it 'was approved by the FDA in 2010 as Nuedexta'.

records.quote: Although the mechanism of action of DM/Q is not fully characterized, its unique properties as an NMDA receptor antagonist and as a Sigma 1 receptor agonist
records.notes: The mechanism is stated for the combination product, not for dextromethorphan or quinidine separately. Also in table 3 on PDF page 303 ('Sigma 1 agonist').

records.quote: DM/Q is a sigma 1 agonist and binds to SERT.
records.notes: The book states binding only and gives no direction (inhibitor or other), so this record may fall outside the strict definition of a mechanism of action; it is kept so that a later reader can decide. The book does not expand 'SERT'; that it is a transporter is an inference. The page mentions 'Binding data' (Werling, et al 2007) but prints no values.

records.quote: Blocking or moderating excessive glutamate neurotransmission with NMDA antagonists may prevent or mitigate damage, maladaptive neurodevelopment or neurodegenerative processes.
records.notes: Class-level record, no compound in this sentence. Table 2 on PDF page 301 lists the class as 'NMDA Antagonists And Glutamatergic'; table 3 on PDF page 303 has the heading 'Drugs with Glutaminergic Effects, AMPA Modulators and NMDA Antagonists'. Members named by the book (memantine, dextromethorphan/quinidine) have their own records.

chapter_notes: Clinical review chapter; all mechanisms are qualitative. No IC50, Ki, EC50, Kd or pharmacokinetic values are printed; the only numbers attached to compounds are clinical case-study doses (risperidone, aripiprazole; also carbamazepine 200 mg ER and Concerta 36 mg on PDF pages 316-317, which have no mechanism record). Most mechanism statements are in table 3 (PDF pages 302-303); tables 4 to 12 (PDF pages 304-312) are lists of clinical-trial titles with no mechanisms. Not recorded because no molecular target or no direction is named: divalproex sodium ('may act by increasing gamma-aminobutyric acid levels in the brain'), acamprosate (reduces glutamate and enhances GABA neurotransmission), methylphenidate ('central nervous system (CNS) stimulant'), choline ('Precursor to Acetylcholine'), sapropterin, N acetylcysteine, 'sigma 1 ligands' (PDF page 300), and compounds that appear only in trial titles (for example galantamine in table 9, arbaclofen/STX209 in table 10, naltrexone, mecamylamine, bumetanide, CX516 in table 12). Reference list starts on PDF page 321; PDF page 324 holds its last entry.
